title: Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Post-Training — Collective Alignment (User Signals)
desc:
About the Team

The Collective Alignment (User Signals) team is a post-training research team working at the intersection of data science, human feedback, and reinforcement learning. We develop methods for learning from real-world user interactions to build AI systems that deliver lasting value, helping people learn, grow, and accomplish increasingly complex goals with ChatGPT.

Learning from user feedback presents fundamental research challenges: signals are often noisy, biased, and difficult to interpret, and improvements in offline metrics do not always translate into better experiences for users. Our team develops scientific approaches to understanding these signals and translating them into improvements in model behavior through evaluations, reward modeling, and post-training.

About the Role

As a Research Engineer or Research Scientist, you will investigate how AI systems can learn from human feedback and real-world usage to better serve users over time.

You will develop new approaches to extracting meaningful learning signals from complex user interactions and incorporating those signals into model training.

This role requires strong deep learning research skills, scientific rigor, and curiosity about how people interact with AI. You will design controlled experiments and ablations, critically examine the relationship between offline evaluations and online model behavior, and work closely with research, product, and data science teams to understand whether improvements translate into meaningful value for users.

In this role, you will:

 - Develop novel methods for learning from human feedback and user interaction signals.

 - Research approaches to incorporating feedback into reward modeling, reinforcement learning, and post-training.

 - Design rigorous experiments and ablation studies to isolate the effects of new data, objectives, and training methods.

 - Develop offline evaluations and investigate their relationship with online experiments and real-world user outcomes.

 - Analyze unexpected results, investigate discrepancies between evaluation metrics and user behavior, and develop hypotheses to guide further research.

 - Evaluate tradeoffs and regressions to improve targeted model behaviors while preserving broader capabilities.

 - Collaborate with research, alignment, product, and data science teams.

 - Implement and debug experiments across large-scale deep learning research systems.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have a strong background in deep learning research through academic or industry experience.

 - Have demonstrated research ability through publications or substantive research contributions in deep learning or LLM post-training.

 - Have experience developing new machine learning methods and evaluating them through rigorous, hypothesis-driven experimentation.

 - Think critically about experimental design, measurement, and what evaluation results do and do not establish about model behavior.

 - Are comfortable designing ablations, investigating surprising results, and reasoning about the relationship between offline metrics and real-world outcomes.

 - Have strong programming skills and experience working with complex ML codebases.

 - Are curious about how people interact with AI and how those interactions can inform better models.

Nice to have:

 - Experience with RLHF, reinforcement learning, or modern LLM post-training.

 - Research or demonstrated interest in AI alignment, human feedback, or user signals.

 - Experience with online experimentation, evaluation methodology, or learning from noisy and biased feedback.

 - Experience connecting machine learning research with real-world product behavior.



About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

Hands-on build: an LLM or ML component for the case and the evaluation that proves it works. Foundation skills, whatever your archetype Software craft: write code that is tested, reviewed and documented. Production ownership: own what you ship after launch, including monitoring, incidents and fixes. AI evaluation: define and run evaluations for AI features, and say when AI is not the right tool. AI system security basics: manage access rights and secrets, and guard against prompt injection. Product and business sense: build for users, ship a first version, measure adoption, improve it. Client relationship: explain your choices to clients and manage your part of the project. title: Machine Learning Researcher - Seismic Foundation Models
desc: Viridien ( www.viridiengroup.com ) is an advanced technology, digital and Earth data company that pushes the boundaries of science for a more prosperous and sustainable future. With our ingenuity, drive and deep curiosity we discover new insights, innovations, and solutions that efficiently and responsibly resolve complex natural resource, digital, energy transition and infrastructure challenges. Job details: The role Viridien, a leader in subsurface imaging, has been building seismic foundation models: models that learn representations of the subsurface from one of the largest, highest-quality proprietary seismic data in the industry, and that adapt to many downstream interpretation and imaging tasks with few labels or zero-shot. These models are primarily vision-oriented, treating seismic data as volumetric image data, and we are increasingly exploring multimodal extensions that incorporate additional data types such as well logs, velocity models and geological metadata. The central research challenge is not simply to train larger models, but to determine what the model learns, where it fails, and how to improve its ability to generalize across surveys, geological settings and downstream tasks. Rigorous understanding of what the model learns and where it generalizes is precisely how we earn a model reliable enough to trust on unseen surveys in production. You will work at the intersection of ML research and seismic imaging production, with access to that proprietary dataset and to substantial on-prem GPU capacity. You will own research hypotheses, model implementations and controlled experiments, working closely with geophysicists and geoscience specialists. No prior seismic expertise is required: our geoscientists will support you in building the domain knowledge you need. We welcome strong early-career researchers as well as more experienced ones, with or without a PhD.. Scientific rigor matters more to us than years of experience. What you do • Advance understanding of what a seismic foundation model learns, where it fails, and how to improve its generalization across surveys and geological settings. • Design, implement and improve model architecture, pre-training objectives and training-data strategies. • Establish generalization on independent seismic surveys against meaningful benchmarks and help define the evaluation protocol. • Diagnose model limitations and work with our ML engineers and geoscience specialists to improve reliability. Required • PhD (completed or near completion) in geophysics, applied mathematics, physics, computer science or a related quantitative field, or equivalent demonstrated research experience (e.g., a strong publication or open-source research record, or substantial research work in industry). • Demonstrated depth in computer vision, including vision transformers and self-supervised or representation learning for image or volumetric data, with the ability to justify training objectives and evaluation methods for scientific signal or image data. • Evidence of strong scientific problem-solving: forming testable hypotheses, designing controlled experiments, interpreting results critically, and learning from approaches that do not work. • Strong hands-on PyTorch skills: implementing, debugging and evaluating research models, with experience optimizing training for limited GPU memory and compute. • Ability to collaborate with geoscience specialists and to communicate technical assumptions and limitations clearly. Preferred (a plus, not required) • Experience with large-scale or distributed (multi-GPU / multi-node) training and the data pipelines it depends on. • Experience with multimodal learning or cross-modal representation alignment. • Prior exposure to seismic, geophysical or other scientific imaging data • Experience taking research models toward production or deployment. • Publications at strong machine-learning or scientific venues, or meaningful open-source contributions. • Familiarity with foundation-model pre-training at scale. What we offer • Access to one of the largest, highest-quality proprietary seismic datasets in the industry. • Substantial dedicated on-prem GPU capacity. • A genuine research mandate to turn advanced FWI imaging into actionable exploration insights and drilling prospects. Houston Benefits: 401k Retirement Plan - when you contribute up to 5%, not only will we match that, but we will also add an additional 2% Free on-site fitness centre offering group exercise classes Short-term disability and long-term disability coverage at no cost to you Parental Leave Program allowing mothers and fathers to take time off from work for childbirth, adoption and to bond with your new child Pet Insurance – options to meet every budget Wellness Program – resources provided to support your personal wellness and participation in activities can earn you $65 quarterly. If you require any reasonable adjustments to fully participate in the application or interview stages, please don’t hesitate to contact your recruiter directly. We see things differently. title: Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Health
desc:
About the Team

The Health team, within OpenAI’s broader Post Training organization, has a mission to ensure AGI improves health for all humanity.

Improving human health will be one of the defining impacts of AGI. Hundreds of millions of people already turn to ChatGPT for questions about their health and millions of clinicians use it weekly to support care delivery. Increasingly capable models create an opportunity to make high-quality medical intelligence more accessible across patients and clinicians—raising the floor of human health—and accelerate the new capabilities and scientific advances that raise the ceiling of human health.

Our job is to make those benefits real. We work across the full model stack—pretraining, midtraining, reinforcement learning, post-training, evaluations, harnessing, and deployment—and connect that research to the patients, clinicians, and real-world outcomes we aim to improve.

About the Role

We’re looking for an exceptional, hands-on researcher who wants to build frontier health capabilities and turn them into impact at scale. This is a role for someone who can take an important, underdefined problem from 0→1: identify the right bet, build what’s needed to test it, and drive it all the way to a measurable improvement in the models and products we actually ship.

We’re especially excited about two kinds of people: researchers with the technical depth to move the frontier in pretraining, reinforcement learning (RL) / post-training, or evals; and researchers with real depth in developing frontier biomedical AI capabilities. Prior experience in healthcare is helpful but not required. Research excellence, velocity, ownership, and alignment with the mission are most important to us.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Own a high-leverage research direction end to end—from deciding which problem matters and how to measure it, to designing and running experiments, to integrating successful work into frontier models.

 - Develop scalable methods across pretraining, midtraining, reinforcement learning, and post-training to improve health reasoning, knowledge, reliability, calibration, and behavior.

 - Build and study RL environments grounded in real health problems; understand which data and training setups produce robust, generalizable improvements rather than just higher benchmark scores.

 - Create meaningful, trustworthy, and unsaturated evaluations that tell us whether our models are actually getting better at what matters for patients and clinicians.

 - Advance new 0→1 capabilities in health that may have an increasing impact with upcoming increases in model intelligence and test-time compute.

 - Develop models and agents that can work over longitudinal, multimodal health data to produce useful predictions, surface new scientific insights, and support better individual- and population-level decisions.

 - Work closely with researchers, engineers, clinicians, and product teams to bring health capabilities into the models and products used by hundreds of millions of people.

 - Help establish that AI improves real health outcomes, not just that it can produce impressive answers or demos.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Care deeply about using increasingly capable AI to improve human health, and take seriously the responsibility of deploying it safely.

 - Have an unusually strong track record in machine learning or AI research, with the depth to push at least one important area forward: pretraining, reinforcement learning / post-training, evals (not necessarily specific to health); or substantial depth in a relevant frontier health / biomedical AI problem.

 - Are a hands-on builder: you can design experiments, write and debug code, work directly with data and training infrastructure, and move quickly from an idea to evidence.

 - Have strong research taste and can distinguish an important problem or a promising approach from an interesting one.

 - Own ambiguous problems end to end, and are willing to learn whatever is missing to get the job done.

 - Stay goal-oriented rather than method-oriented, and don’t shy away from unglamorous work if it is the highest-leverage path to impact.

 - Care about whether a capability will scale, generalize, and make it into the real world—not just whether it can be shown in a paper or prototype.

 - Enjoy working with low-ego, ambitious people across research, engineering, medicine, and product.

 - Bonus: Experience with health AI, longitudinal health data, or clinical research.

desc: Chez Alfa Laval Golbey, nous concevons et fabriquons des échangeurs thermiques de haute technologie utilisés dans les secteurs de l’énergie, du GNL et des industries de process. Notre savoir-faire reconnu en cryogénie nous permet d’accompagner des projets industriels majeurs à l’échelle internationale. Rejoindre notre site de Golbey, c’est intégrer un environnement industriel stimulant, au sein d’un groupe international innovant, engagé dans la performance durable et la transition énergétique. Quel est le poste ? Dans le cadre de la modernisation de sa méthode de dimensionnement des échangeurs à plaques et ailettes brasées en aluminium, Alfa Laval Golbey souhaite évaluer l’apport de méthodes de type Intelligence Artificielle / Machine Learning. Dans ce cadre, une première étape consistant à construire une base de données a d’ores et déjà été réalisée. Cette base de données contient la description des équipements à la fois d’un point de vue géométrique, mais aussi du point de vue des conditions de fonctionnement. Nous recherchons un stagiaire R&D (H/F) pour poursuivre cette démarche. Vos missions seront de : Identifier les variables les plus explicatives pour prédire les caractéristiques géométriques des équipements Entrainer, sur la base de données existante, plusieurs modèles visant à prédire certaines caractéristiques géométriques des échangeurs lors de la phase de design de l’équipement Adapter et compléter la base de données pour améliorer la prédiction des modèles, que ce soit par l’ajout de nouvelles variables dans la base de données ou par l’estimation de nouvelles variables à partir de celles déjà disponibles (nombres adimensionnels, …) Ce stage permettra donc d’identifier clairement les apports et limites de telles méthodes, mais également celles associées à la base de données actuellement disponible. Ce travail contribuera au développement d’une nouvelle approche de dimensionnement des échangeurs de chaleur à plaques et ailettes brasées s’appuyant, d’une part, sur des approches physiques et, d’autre part, sur une approche « data » pour améliorer et accélérer le processus de conception en identifiant plus rapidement une géométrie adéquate. Une compréhension de l’approche physique et des échanges réguliers au sein de l’équipe permettront de conduire en parallèle ces deux axes de développement. Qui êtes-vous ? Que connaissez-vous ? Actuellement en Master 2, Ecole d’ingénieur ou équivalent, vous avez une orientation sur l’analyse de données, ou le Machine Learning. Des notions de thermiques et de mécanique des fluides seraient un peu plus pour mieux appréhender le fonctionnement de l’équipement et les relations entre les différentes informations stockées dans la base de données. Vous avez également une forte sensibilisation à l’Intelligence Artificielle, aux outils de Machine Learning et à Python. Votre capacité de communication et votre curiosité vous permettront de mener à bien cette mission. Durée du stage : 6 mois à partir de février ou mars 2027 Pourquoi nous rejoindre ? Nous offrons un poste stimulant dans un environnement ouvert et convivial où nous nous aidons mutuellement à nous développer et à créer de la valeur. Votre travail aura un véritable impact sur le succès futur d’Alfa Laval. En nous rejoignant, vous intégrerez un groupe international qui vous donnera accès à de multiples opportunités d’évolution et de mobilité, et ce, dans de nombreux domaines professionnels, notamment grâce à nos programmes d’intégration et d’accompagnement, mais également sur le plan personnel. En effet, vous pourrez bénéficier d’un mode de travail hybride et de nombreux autres avantages mutuelle, restaurant d’entreprise, CE, accord d’intéressement et de participation, etc.

About Prosper AI

Prosper is building the most advanced conversational AI agents for healthcare — human-like phone agents that handle the administrative work draining the system: claims status checks, benefit verification, prior authorizations, patient scheduling, and balance reminders. Our mission is to eliminate $200B in administrative waste so healthcare professionals can focus more on healing and less on paperwork.

What you'll do

At Prosper, we’re pushing the limits of what’s possible with real-time AI. We’re not just making voice agents that “talk”, we’re engineering systems that sound human, reason under strong latency constraints, and adapt instantly to messy, high-stakes healthcare conversations. As a Software Engineer, you’ll be at the center of designing and scaling our platform, the low-latency speech/LLM pipelines, orchestration layers, and reliability systems that make this possible.

 - Be ready to handle the challenges of deploying AI voice agents to thousands of daily phone calls.

 - Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Maths, Physics or related field (or equivalent experience).
